selected_evidence.summary: /srv/secure mounted from /dev/mapper/secure_srv (LUKS-backed), healthcheck.txt written with known SHA-256, pre-restart boot_id=31b01b46-96de-4ded-a021-49887e7d4053 captured

selected_evidence.requirement: Auto-unlock/auto-mount configuration in place (crypttab + fstab with systemd dependency) validated before reboot
selected_evidence.summary: crypttab (noauto luks entry) and fstab (x-systemd.requires=systemd-cryptsetup@secure_srv.service) entries added; manually starting srv-secure.mount unit correctly triggered the cryptsetup dependency and mounted the volume, proving the wiring works
systemctl reboot issued via backgrounded/delayed subshell so the exec call returned REBOOT_TRIGGERED before the node went down

selected_evidence.requirement: Node restart confirmed unreachable then reachable again, with changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Immediately after reboot trigger, exec timed out (node down); subsequent poll succeeded with new boot_id=b22cc786-326c-4cfa-826e-133f121ad6ec (differs from baseline) and new uptime-since timestamp

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: encrypted volume auto-unlocked, mounted, and data intact without manual intervention
selected_evidence.summary: Post-boot, systemd-cryptsetup@secure_srv.service and srv-secure.mount both show Active since the boot time (auto-started, no manual commands run), /srv/secure is mounted from /dev/mapper/secure_srv, and healthcheck.txt SHA-256 matches the pre-restart baseline exactly
